proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
N_\star=n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}.
\]
We first prove termination and exclusivity of the output.  By \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}alphabet}\), every alphabet over which either special branch forms a displayed sum is finite.  The first and second rules of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) compare the input with fixed finite templates.  The third rule computes ancestry, descendants, simple paths, and directed cycles in the finite graph \(H\); if its predicate is true, it constructs the finite set \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L,X)\) and a sum over its finite product alphabet.  Thus each of the first three rules is a terminating finite computation.

If the fourth rule is reached and the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and loop-free, \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
A^\star\subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0]
\quad\text{and}\quad
|A^\star|\le n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}=N_\star.
\]
An ID memo state assigns to every vertex of \(A^\star\) one of the three labels absent, random, or fixed.  Hence the number of possible memo states is at most
\[
3^{|A^\star|}\le 3^{N_\star}.
\]
The fourth rule in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) never revisits a memo state, so its ordinary-ID call terminates after at most \(3^{N_\star}\) memo transitions.  Counting one initialization and at most four ordered top-level rule evaluations gives the bound
\[
1+4+3^{N_\star}
=5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}
=B_\star(n,L,\gamma).
\]
The rules are ordered and deterministic, every successful match returns immediately, and every residual case returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).  Therefore precisely one of \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A))\), and \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) is emitted within the stated bound.

We next prove the claimed semantics of every success, considering all success-producing rules.  If the first rule matches, the input is exactly \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), including \(x=0\) and \(y=1\).  By \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\), for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\),
\[
F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)
=P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0))
=\theta_M(1;0).
\]
The same proposition displays \(F_{\mathrm{out}}\) as a finite sum of observed conditional probabilities.  By \(\mathrm{ass:cylinder\text{-}positivity}\), every conditioning-cylinder denominator in that display is positive; rewriting each conditional probability as a ratio of two cylinder probabilities therefore proves
\[
F_{\mathrm{out}}\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}}).
\]

If neither special rule matches and the third-rule predicate \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) is true, \(\mathrm{prop:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}transfer}\) yields, simultaneously,
\[
F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x)=\theta_M(y;x)
\quad\text{for every }M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A).
\]
That proposition applies without imposing acyclicity or absence of self-loops on the directed summary, so it covers every eligible cyclic or self-looped input admitted by the third rule.

Finally, suppose the fourth rule returns an ordinary-ID expression \(F\).  Its graphical precondition is exactly that the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and loop-free.  Therefore \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) applies and gives
\[
F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)
\quad\text{for every }M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A).
\]
These are all rules that can emit \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}\), so every success has the asserted uniform identifying property.

There is exactly one failure-producing rule, namely the second special rule.  When it matches, \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\) supplies the displayed rational structural tables on the unchanged binary alphabet.  By \(\mathrm{prop:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}collision}\), those tables define final models satisfying
\[
M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A),
\qquad
P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\quad\text{as measures on }\Omega_{\mathcal A},
\]
while their target values obey
\[
\theta_{M_0}(1;0)=\frac{13}{50}
\ne
\frac12=\theta_{M_1}(1;0).
\]
Thus the emitted finite lag-switch certificate has exactly the model-membership, common-law, and effect-separation properties claimed for every failure.  The conclusion \(\operatorname{UID}(H,1,\mathcal A,1,3,1,0,1)=0\) also follows directly from \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\); equivalently, it is certified by \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\) applied to this pair.

It remains to establish the general semantic implications of the output tags.  Suppose first that the procedure emits \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), and take arbitrary \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) such that \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).  Equality of the measures implies equality of every cylinder probability occurring in the finite expression \(F\).  All denominators used by \(F\) are positive by the definition of \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) and \(\mathrm{ass:cylinder\text{-}positivity}\), so substitution into that expression gives
\[
F(P_{M_0})=F(P_{M_1}).
\]
Success soundness then gives
\[
\theta_{M_0}(y;x)=F(P_{M_0})=F(P_{M_1})=\theta_{M_1}(y;x).
\]
Since the pair was arbitrary, \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\) yields \(\operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=1\).  If the procedure emits \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), the certified pair just constructed has a common observed law and unequal targets, so the implication defining \(\operatorname{UID}=1\) is false and \(\operatorname{UID}=0\).  All inputs not covered by one of the sound success rules or the single direct failure rule reach \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) by \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\).  This proves the stated one-way implications and, because no inference is made from \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\), proves exactly the advertised absence of either converse.

Assume \(L=0\).  Since the query lag satisfies \(0\le\gamma\le L\),
\[
\gamma=0.
\]
Let \(R\in\mathfrak R(H,0)\).  By \(\mathrm{def:refinement\text{-}class}\), \(R\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:refinement\text{-}span}\), and hence every directed edge has the form \(i_t\to j_t\) and every bidirected edge has the form \(i_t\leftrightarrow j_t\).  The translation invariance in the definition of a stationary refinement implies, for every \(k\in\mathbb Z\),
\[
i_t\to j_t\in E_{\to}(R)
\iff i_{t+k}\to j_{t+k}\in E_{\to}(R),
\]
and likewise
\[
i_t\leftrightarrow j_t\in E_{\leftrightarrow}(R)
\iff i_{t+k}\leftrightarrow j_{t+k}\in E_{\leftrightarrow}(R).
\]
Consequently \(R\) is the translation closure of its time-zero mixed graph on \(V\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:exact\text{-}summary}\), the directed and bidirected coordinate pairs in that time-zero graph are exactly those in \(H\).  Thus every feasible refinement is the translation closure of one finite static ADMG on \(V\) (indeed, of the static mixed graph represented by \(H\)).

Moreover, if \(H^{\to}\) contained a directed cycle through distinct vertices, its time-zero copy would be a directed cycle in the instantaneous slice of \(R\); if it contained a directed self-loop, its time-zero copy would be a self-loop in that slice.  Either event contradicts \(\mathrm{ass:instantaneous\text{-}acyclicity}\).  Therefore
\[
H^{\to}\text{ is acyclic and has no directed self-loop}.
\]

The first two rules of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) require their displayed lag-one inputs, whereas the present input has \(L=0\).  Hence neither special rule can match.  If
\[
\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,0)=\mathsf{true},
\]
the third rule returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\).  By \(\mathrm{prop:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}transfer}\),
\[
F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x)=\theta_M(y;x)
\quad\text{for every }M\in\mathfrak M(H,0,\mathcal A).
\]
This proves the claimed uniformly valid adjustment outcome.

Suppose instead that the adjustment predicate is false.  The acyclic and loop-free property proved above makes the fourth rule applicable.  Because \(L=\gamma=0\), the ancestor-window conclusion of \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) becomes
\[
A^\star\subseteq V\times[0,0].
\]
Hence the saturated time-unrolled ancestral graph has only time-zero vertices and is precisely the relevant ancestral subgraph of the common static ADMG.  By \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\), the procedure makes one memoized ordinary-ID call on this graph.  If ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)
\quad\text{and}\quad
F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)
\quad\text{for every }M\in\mathfrak M(H,0,\mathcal A),
\]
so the rule returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\) on the common product alphabet.  If ID fails, the same rule returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).  In particular, the definition contains no operation converting this ID failure into a lag-switch certificate, and \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\) assigns no semantic conclusion to \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).  Therefore no fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is claimed on the ID-failure branch, as required.
